claims.text: The initial composite consists of discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments embedded in a Cu matrix.
The untreated W–Cu composite exhibits phase separation under the relevant processing or service conditions.
The untreated W–Cu composite forms interfacial voids under the relevant processing or service conditions.
A nanoscale Ni interlayer can be applied to W surfaces before composite consolidation.
The Ni interlayer will suppress phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
The Ni interlayer will suppress interfacial void formation in the W–Cu composite.
The Ni interlayer improves wettability at the W–Cu interface.
The Ni interlayer improves bonding between the W and Cu phases.
The Ni interlayer forms a graded interface during sintering.
Formation of the Ni-containing graded interface promotes interdiffusion between W and Cu.
Enhanced interdiffusion and bonding stabilize the microstructure against phase separation.
Enhanced interdiffusion and bonding reduce void formation during heat-transfer and irradiation exposure.
The Ni-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable untreated W–Cu composite.
The proposed effect is applicable under elevated heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing material and Cu-based cooling-component joints.
Beneficial performance requires sintering parameters that support interdiffusion without compromising composite integrity.
